canonical_task: computable in P by greedy edge selection
citation: Miyano, The lexicographically first maximal subgraph problems, Int. J. Found. Comput. Sci. 1 (1990)

canonical_task: unit propagation to fixpoint, poly-time
citation: Greenlaw, Hoover & Ruzzo, Limits to Parallel Computation: P-Completeness Theory (1995)

canonical_task: abelian stabilization is order-independent, poly-time
citation: Bjorner, Lovasz & Shor, Chip-firing games on graphs, Eur. J. Combin. 12 (1991)

canonical_task: greedy LZ78 dictionary parse, poly-time
citation: De Agostino & Storer, On-line versus off-line computation in dynamic text compression, Inf. Proc. Lett. 59 (1996)

canonical_task: lex-first greedy (Delta+1)-coloring is P-complete
citation: Greenlaw, Hoover & Ruzzo, Limits to Parallel Computation: P-Completeness Theory (1995)

canonical_task: Subgraph Isomorphism decision (H a subgraph of G)
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)
note: GJ [GT48]; generalizes CLIQUE and HAMILTONIAN-CYCLE. Distinct from induced-subgraph-isomorphism (induced) and graph-isomorphism (S2)

canonical_task: 3-Partition decision: a partition into m triples each summing to B?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Complexity results for multiprocessor scheduling under resource constraints, SIAM J. Comput. 4 (1975) 397-411; Garey & Johnson (1979) [SP15]
note: the canonical STRONGLY NP-complete problem: NP-hard even with all integers bounded by a polynomial in m (unary). Distinct from Partition (2-way, weakly NP-complete) and Numerical 3-Dimensional Matchin

canonical_task: Bandwidth decision: is there a layout of bandwidth <= b?
citation: Papadimitriou, The NP-completeness of the bandwidth minimization problem, Computing 16 (1976) 263-270
note: NP-complete (Papadimitriou 1976), even for trees (Garey-Graham-Johnson-Knuth 1978). Distinct from cutwidth / minimum linear arrangement (S2)

canonical_task: Clique-width decision: cwd(G) <= k?
citation: Fellows, Rosamond, Rotics & Szeider, Clique-width is NP-complete, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 23 (2009) 909-939 (STOC 2006)
note: NP-complete (Fellows-Rosamond-Rotics-Szeider 2009), resolving a question open since clique-width was introduced. Distinct from treewidth / rank-width (S2)

canonical_task: Crossing Number decision: a drawing with <= k crossings?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Crossing number is NP-complete, SIAM J. Algebraic Discrete Methods 4 (1983) 312-316
note: NP-complete (Garey-Johnson 1983). Distinct from planarity (crossing number 0, poly-time) and from the rectilinear crossing number (S2)

canonical_task: Metric UFL decision: an open-set + assignment of total cost <= B?
citation: NP-hard via Set Cover / Dominating Set (Cornuejols, Nemhauser & Wolsey, The uncapacitated facility location problem, in Discrete Location Theory (1990)); Garey & Johnson 1979
note: NP-hard (metric). Distinct from capacitated facility location and from k-median (no opening costs, cardinality bound) (S2)

canonical_task: MIS on unit-disk graphs decision: independent set of size >= k? NP-complete
citation: Clark, Colbourn & Johnson, Unit disk graphs, Discrete Mathematics 86 (1990) 165-177
note: MIS is NP-complete on unit-disk graphs

canonical_task: Independent Dominating Set decision: independent dominating set of size <= k? NP-complete
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)
note: minimum maximal independent set / independent domination is NP-complete

canonical_task: Map Labelling decision: common label size >= sigma achievable? NP-complete
citation: Formann & Wagner, A packing problem with applications to lettering of maps, Proc. 7th ACM Symposium on Computational Geometry (SoCG) 1991, 281-288

canonical_task: MMVC decision: a minimal vertex cover of size >= k? NP-complete
citation: Boria, Della Croce & Paschos, On the max min vertex cover problem, Discrete Applied Mathematics 196 (2015) 62-71
note: the maximization dual of minimum independent domination; NP-complete

canonical_task: MCSP decision: a common partition into <= k blocks?
citation: Goldstein, Kolman & Zheng, Minimum common string partition problem: hardness and approximations, Electron. J. Combin. 12 (2005) R50
note: NP-hard, even when each letter occurs at most twice (2-MCSP)

canonical_task: Minimum Latency decision: a tour with total latency <= L?
citation: Blum, Chalasani, Coppersmith, Pulleyblank, Raghavan & Sudan, The minimum latency problem, STOC 1994, 163-171
note: NP-hard on metric spaces (Blum et al. 1994)

canonical_task: Nearest Codeword decision: a codeword within Hamming distance d of y?
citation: Berlekamp, McEliece & van Tilborg, On the inherent intractability of certain coding problems, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 24 (1978) 384-386
note: maximum-likelihood decoding of a linear code is NP-complete (BMvT 1978)

canonical_task: Planar Vertex Deletion decision: a set of <= k vertices whose removal yields a planar graph?
citation: Lewis & Yannakakis, The node-deletion problem for hereditary properties is NP-complete, JCSS 20 (1980) 219-230
note: vertex deletion to any nontrivial hereditary property (here planarity) is NP-complete

canonical_task: L(2,1) span decision: is lambda(G) <= k?
citation: Griggs & Yeh, Labelling graphs with a condition at distance 2, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 5 (1992) 586-595
note: determining the L(2,1) span is NP-complete

canonical_task: Set Splitting feasibility: a 2-coloring splitting every set (hypergraph 2-colorability)?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [SP4]
note: NP-complete even for sets of size 3 (Lovasz); equivalently hypergraph 2-colorability / Property B

canonical_task: HP folding decision: a self-avoiding embedding with >= k H-H contacts?
citation: Berger & Leighton, Protein folding in the hydrophobic-hydrophilic (HP) model is NP-complete, J. Comput. Biol. 5 (1998) 27-40

canonical_task: Triangle Packing decision: >= k vertex-disjoint triangles? (Partition into Triangles is the exact version)
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [GT11 Partition into Triangles]

canonical_task: P||sum w_j C_j decision: a schedule with weighted completion time <= V?
citation: Bruno, Coffman & Sethi, Scheduling independent tasks to reduce mean finishing time, Comm. ACM 17 (1974) 382-387
note: NP-hard already for m=2 (Partition); the single-machine 1||sum w_j C_j is in P (Smith's WSPT rule, S2)

canonical_task: matching existence / maximum matching: a matching always exists (the empty set) and a maximum matching is found in poly time by the blossom algorithm — the decoupling witness (optimization easy, counting hard)
citation: Edmonds, Paths, trees, and flowers, Canad. J. Math. 17 (1965) 449-467
note: maximum matching in poly time (Edmonds 1965); existence is trivial
